findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` with only `pass`. That leaves the abstract members unimplemented: `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` and `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. When `Detector.detector_handler` calls `group_type.detector_handler(self)` for a `metric_alert_fire` detector, Python raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class`. Before this change the class was a concrete no-op handler, so this is a crash that did not exist previously.

findings.title: DetectorPriorityLevel converted to PriorityLevel without validation
findings.body: `PriorityLevel(new_status)` assumes every `DetectorPriorityLevel` value has a matching value in `PriorityLevel`. Any non-OK detector level that does not map (for example a level added only to `DetectorPriorityLevel`) raises `ValueError` mid-evaluation. Because the dedupe update has already been enqueued at that point, the failure leaves enqueued state for that packet that is not consistent with what was actually processed. There is no explicit mapping or check before the conversion.

findings.title: Test builds expected occurrence with wrong value for group_2
findings.body: The expected occurrence for group_2 is built with value 6, but the data packet supplies 10 for group_2. The tests pass only because the mock `build_occurrence_and_event_data` ignores `value`. As a result, nothing verifies that the hook receives the correct per-group value. The same pattern appears in other tests that use 6 for inputs of 8, 100 and 10.
